continuity_scope: Magi: The Labyrinth of Magic, Vol. 1, VIZ English paperback/digital edition (13 August 2013; ISBN 978-1-4215-5951-3; 200 pages), credited to Shinobu Ohtaka. This is a narrow English manga-volume pass. The official Shogakukan Japanese マギ 1 e-comic listing is retained solely as a separate original-language Volume 1 edition boundary, not merged translation evidence.
work_or_witnesses: Magi: The Labyrinth of Magic, Vol. 1, VIZ English paperback/digital edition (13 August 2013)
VIZ Vol. 1 free-preview reader landing page
coverage_rule: Include only named individual dramatic characters directly named by the selected VIZ English Volume 1 product synopsis: Aladdin, his friend Alibaba, and the individualized djinn Ugo. The selected synopsis directly supports Aladdin and Alibaba's friendship and the stated travel companionship with Ugo; no uncaptioned preview panels, later chapter material, or external character roster is inferred. The preview's browser-accessible landing page does not expose searchable page/panel text, so claims remain at official-metadata level.
omissions: All later VIZ volumes/chapters, the rest of the 37-volume manga series, the original Japanese serialization, spin-offs, games, guidebooks, films, merchandise, and other adaptations are separate witnesses.
The Aniplex television anime is a separately labeled animated production and is not evidence for any record in this manga-volume pass.

The Shogakukan Japanese マギ 1 listing names Aladdin, Laila, and Saasa in a different official Volume 1 synopsis. It is not used to transfer those names, plot details, or wording into this English-edition pass; that witness needs its own Japanese-edition research pass.

Magi/dungeon-capturer designations, peoples, caravan and thief groups, magic, djinn as a category, artifacts, Dungeons, places, and themes are terms/dimensions rather than character nodes unless the selected VIZ witness individually names and describes an agent.
The official English metadata is not sufficient for a full treatment of slavery, oppression, violence, injuries, coercion, or outcomes; no broader-franchise content detail is imported.
uncertainties: VIZ's browser-readable preview gives a primary edition-reader landing page but no practical text/panel locator. It establishes the existence of a Vol. 1 preview, not a transcribed chapter-level evidentiary record.

The VIZ Volume 1 synopsis gives names, Ugo's djinn designation, Aladdin/Alibaba friendship, travel setup, dunes, and fortune-seeking, but not ages, origins, abilities, exact Dungeon mechanics, individual motives, or outcomes.

VIZ says the series is inspired by One Thousand and One Nights. This is an influence statement only: neither shared continuity nor identity/equivalence with traditional Arabic-language story characters, cultural contexts, or historical traditions is asserted.

Adventure-danger, exploitation/slavery and oppression themes, and violence may arise in the wider franchise, but this selected metadata supports only a Teen-rated desert/dungeon premise. Those subjects are flagged as boundaries/content cautions rather than asserted plot facts.
No relationship is inferred between Alibaba and Ugo merely because both accompany Aladdin in the synopsis.
evidence_basis: VIZ first-party English Volume 1 product/preview and series metadata, with Shogakukan and Aniplex first-party pages used only to document edition and adaptation separation. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, anime recap, external translation, or uninspected panel transcription is used as character evidence.
